blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, tax and compliance stop being technical work and become strategic leadership. The question is not whether the team can file correctly — that is assumed — but how the company positions itself within the rules, how it manages relationships with regulators over years, and how it responds when the rules change in the middle of a period.

Good senior tax leadership is almost boring on a day-to-day basis. The calendar is steady, filings are on time, and borderline positions are documented and reviewed by legal counsel. Relationships with tax authorities are built in calm times, so that when a difficult question arrives, there is already a direct line to the right person.

Although regulators rarely comment on the companies that get this right, they notice the ones that do not. The quiet cost of tax missteps — reputational, financial, and political — is almost always higher than the short-term saving that caused them. Senior tax leadership is the art of never becoming an interesting case study.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level the central question about tax is NOT whether the team can file correctly, but rather…
options: how the company positions itself within the rules
how quickly the team can submit each return
how many people the compliance function requires
which software the finance team should adopt
items.why: "The question is not whether the team can file correctly… but how the company positions itself within the rules." A competência técnica é dada como certa.

items.q: When are relationships with tax authorities built, according to the passage?
options: After a misstep has already occurred
During the annual audit season
In calm times, before they are needed
Only when a difficult question arrives
items.why: "Relationships with tax authorities are built in calm times, so that when a difficult question arrives, there is already a direct line."

items.q: The author describes good senior tax leadership as "almost boring on a day-to-day basis." This phrasing most strongly suggests that…
options: senior tax leaders are underqualified for their roles
the work is genuinely unimportant to the company
the discipline should be automated as soon as possible
steadiness and the absence of drama are signs of it being done well
items.why: Inferência: o "tédio" é elogio — calendário estável, tudo em dia. A ausência de crises é o resultado de um bom trabalho.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Borderline positions should be documented and reviewed by legal counsel.
Regulators pay closer attention to companies that handle tax poorly.
Reputational damage from tax missteps can outweigh the money saved.
A short-term tax saving is worth pursuing even if it draws regulator scrutiny.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que "the quiet cost… is almost always higher than the short-term saving that caused them" — logo, o autor discordaria de perseguir essa economia.

items.q: The closing line — "the art of never becoming an interesting case study" — implies that being noticed by regulators is…
options: the primary goal of tax leadership
unavoidable for any large organisation
an outcome the company should quietly avoid
a mark of prestige for the finance team
items.why: Inferência: "they notice the ones that do not" get it right. Virar estudo de caso significa ter errado — algo a evitar, não a exibir.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando sobre o trabalho de reconstruir a relação com o regulador. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, where things stand. The misunderstanding itself was minor — a classification question on one filing, nothing that touches the numbers in any material way. But minor things become expensive when they are handled defensively, and I would rather over-invest in this now than have it linger.

I met their regional lead on Tuesday. No lawyers in the room, no theatre — just the two documents, laid out, and an honest account of how we read the rule. What I wanted her to leave with was a simple impression: that we are the kind of company that picks up the phone before there is a problem, not after.

Here is my thinking. We do not have a relationship yet that we can draw on, and that is precisely the gap. When a genuinely hard question lands next year — and one always does — I want a direct line to someone who already trusts how we work. You cannot build that trust in the middle of a dispute; it has to exist beforehand.

None of this shows up in a report. Nobody upstairs will ever see the meeting that did not turn into a crisis. That is rather the point of the job.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Charlotte characterise the misunderstanding itself?
options: A serious error that changed the reported numbers
A dispute that has already reached the courts
A deliberate attempt to save money on one filing
A minor classification question with no material impact
items.why: "The misunderstanding itself was minor — a classification question on one filing, nothing that touches the numbers in any material way."

items.q: Why did Charlotte choose to meet the regional lead with no lawyers present?
options: To make the meeting cheaper to run
To keep the meeting informal, honest, and free of theatre
Because the company was not permitted to bring lawyers
Because legal counsel was unavailable that week
items.why: "No lawyers in the room, no theatre — just the two documents… and an honest account."

items.q: What impression did Charlotte most want the regulator to leave with?
options: That the finance team is larger than the regulator assumed
That the company picks up the phone before there is a problem
That the classification question was the regulator's fault
That the company disputes the rule and will fight it
items.why: "that we are the kind of company that picks up the phone before there is a problem, not after."

items.q: When Charlotte says "you cannot build that trust in the middle of a dispute; it has to exist beforehand," she is implying that…
options: disputes should be avoided by never contacting regulators
the value of the relationship is realised later, when a hard question arrives
the current meeting is itself a dispute
trust is irrelevant once a dispute begins
items.why: Inferência: ela investe agora para ter uma linha direta quando "a genuinely hard question lands next year" — o retorno é futuro.

items.q: What does Charlotte suggest about the visibility of this work inside her own company?
options: It will be celebrated in the next board report
It will only be recognised if the regulator praises it
It is closely monitored by senior leadership
It is largely invisible — the crisis that never happens goes unnoticed
items.why: Inferência: "Nobody upstairs will ever see the meeting that did not turn into a crisis. That is rather the point of the job."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The desk took a borderline position on the deduction and flagged it for review." A borderline position is…
options: a position agreed in advance with the regulator
a treatment that sits near the edge of what the rules allow
a filing submitted after the deadline
a stance that clearly breaks the rules
items.why: Borderline position = posição limítrofe: defensável, mas próxima do limite do que a regra permite — por isso é documentada e revisada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before adopting the aggressive treatment, the CFO asked ___ to confirm it would hold up."
options: the regulator
legal counsel
the direct line
the case study
items.why: Legal counsel = assessoria jurídica: quem valida se a posição se sustenta juridicamente.

items.q: "A single misstep on disclosure cost the firm two years of goodwill." A misstep is…
options: a long-term strategic advantage
a formal approval from a regulator
a routine, on-time filing
a small error or wrong move with disproportionate consequences
items.why: Misstep = tropeço: um erro ou passo em falso cujo custo excede em muito o tamanho aparente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Chasing a ___ on this quarter's rate is not worth inviting an audit that could drag on for years."
options: short-term saving
case study
legal counsel
calm time
items.why: Short-term saving = economia de curto prazo: o ganho imediato que, segundo a lição, quase nunca compensa o risco reputacional.

items.q: "Because she had cultivated a direct line to the authority, the query was resolved in a single call." A direct line here means…
options: a trusted, personal channel to the right decision-maker
a dedicated phone number for public complaints
a formal legal appeal process
a straight-line reporting hierarchy inside the firm
items.why: Direct line = linha direta: acesso confiável à pessoa certa, construído em tempos calmos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de estratégia tributária e compliance. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal will need to sign off on the disclosure before we file." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve it
circulate it for comments
delay it until next quarter
translate it for the regulator
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final antes de seguir adiante.

items.q: "When the rule changed mid-period, the team had to get ahead of the regulator." To get ahead of something means to…
options: ignore it until it becomes urgent
overtake a competitor's filing
act on it early, before it turns into a problem
escalate it to the board immediately
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se: agir cedo para controlar a situação antes que ela vire crise.

items.q: "The auditors pushed back on our classification of the receivable." They…
options: rewrote the whole return
resisted or challenged it
postponed the review
approved it without question
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — questionar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed a remediation plan but never followed through on it." This means we…
options: carried it out to completion
documented it thoroughly
handed it to another department
failed to see it through to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; sem isso, o plano fica só no papel.

items.q: "A one-point rate cut sounds attractive, but it won't move the needle once you weigh the exposure." To move the needle means to…
options: make a noticeable, meaningful difference
reduce the workload of the team
shift the deadline forward
trigger a regulatory audit
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro: produzir uma diferença perceptível e relevante.
